entities.summary: François-Noël Babeuf, also known as Gracchus Babeuf, was a French proto-communist, revolutionary, and journalist of the French Revolutionary period. His newspaper Le Tribun du Peuple was best known for its advocacy for the poor and calling for a popular revolt against the Directory, the government of France. He was a leading advocate for democracy and the abolition of private property. He made his own variant of Jacobinism (Robespierrism) which is called Neo-Jacobinism. Besides the influence of Robespierrism on his thought, due to his proto-communism, his political views were more aligned with the ideology of the Enragés.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Babeufism's advocacy for democracy and abolition of private property influenced the French Revolution's emphasis on social equality, contributing to the eventual rise of Napoleon Bonaparte. His ideas also shaped the development of modern communism.
